newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOCCER-INJURIES HIT CYPRUS AHEAD OF RUSSIA CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURIES HIT CYPRUS AHEAD OF RUSSIA CLASH.

text.p: Cyprus may be forced by a spate of injuries to make changes for Saturday's World Cup match against Russia, their first qualifier since losing to Bulgaria in a game that led to match-rigging claims.
At least seven probables are out, and coach Stavros Papadopoulos said on Wednesday: "We have some problems with injuries. We will assess the situation and we may be bringing in new players."
Papadopoulos took over after Andreas Michaelides resigned as coach in January following allegations the match against Bulgaria was rigged. Michaelides cited personal reasons for quitting.
Cyprus lost 3-1 to the Bulgarians in a European group five qualifier in Limassol on December 14, and rumours subsequently surfaced that some players placed high bets for their team to lose.
The claims are now the subject of an official inquiry by the Cyprus Sports Association (KOA).
